clue.text: German dramatist digesting long horror story

indicators.note: a body digesting food holds it inside, so the dramatist's name takes the next word within it

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German playwright
to long or yearn is to pine

explanation.surface: A German playwright tucks into a lengthy tale of terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale that sends shivers down the back is a classic name for a thriller or horror story.

clue.text: Tinker crossing trade centre at a brisk pace

indicators.note: the tinker spans the market, which sits inside his name

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a mart is a market, a centre of trade

explanation.surface: A travelling mender passes through a market quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a verb meaning fiddle; it is Christopher Sly, the tinker of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something smartly means doing it quickly and briskly.

clue.text: Dramatist initially indulged by old nurse

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: SEN, a State Enrolled Nurse, was a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A playwright was spoiled at first by an elderly nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes I and B from 'indulged by'. 'Old' marks SEN as a grade no longer awarded in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Explain details, putting up bundle of hay's old price

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up writes it bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a bale is a bound bundle of hay
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Going into detail about what a bale of hay used to cost.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'putting up' reads the bale from bottom to top, giving ELAB; the 's of hay's is only possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to expand on something by adding fuller explanation.

clue.text: Script producing round of applause

definitions.meaning: handwriting, as in writing in a neat script
a burst of clapping, as in give her a big one

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's handwriting and a round of clapping.

clue.text: Frolic on branch line serving plant

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a frolic
a spur is a short branch line off a main railway

explanation.surface: Having fun on a little railway that delivers flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium-like flowers with a spurred blossom are a garden plant of this name.

clue.text: Former church leader's beginning to be superior

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ex-bishop starts to rise above everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes L from leader's.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo others or shine is to excel.

clue.text: Order worker crossing island to be respectful

indicators.note: the order and worker together span the island, which sits inside them

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Tell a labourer travelling across an island to show some deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is the British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant describes bowing deferentially, showing reverence.

clue.text: Fairly small-minded about resistance

indicators.note: about means around, so the small-minded word surrounds the letter

parts.note: petty means mean-spirited or small-minded
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Rather narrow-minded about any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside PETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means fairly or rather, as in quite good.

clue.text: Abandoned seat in bar, being on the wagon

indicators.note: abandoned behaviour is wild and unrestrained, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who gave up drink sits in a pub but no longer takes a stool there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' rearranges SEATINBAR. 'Being' is a noun here: a being on the wagon is a person who has stopped drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the wagon is an idiom for refusing alcohol, so such a person is a teetotaller.

clue.text: Seeing it in Scotland, Sassenachs may not give a toss!

definitions.text: Seeing it in Scotland, Sassenachs may not give a toss!

parts.words: Seeing it in Scotland, Sassenachs may not give a toss!
parts.note: English visitors to the Highland games may be indifferent, or may be unable to hurl the heavy pole that strong Scots throw end over end

explanation.surface: The English don't care about something they see north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not give a toss' is British slang for not caring, but it also points to the event at Highland games where competitors toss a tree trunk. Sassenach is a Scots word for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy tapered pole thrown in Highland games is the very thing one might not toss.

clue.text: Continue to look after fibrous tissue

parts.note: to look after a patient is to tend them
carry on or go on means continue, so on gives this piece

explanation.surface: Keep caring for a damaged sinew.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord of tough fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone is the anatomical term defined here.

clue.text: Songwriter's stew's eaten by pet, lacking energy

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so the stew sits within the pet
E is the physics symbol for energy, and lacking it removes that letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its E
a salmis is a rich ragout of game birds; the 's here reads as part of the dish's name

explanation.surface: A composer's casserole has been wolfed by the family dog, which is now listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' leaves PT. A salmis is a French game stew, an uncommon word; 'Songwriter's' reads as 'songwriter is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of psalms, such as King David, is a composer of sacred songs.

clue.text: Royal servant longing to consume duck with mother

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed inside, so the longing holds the other pieces

parts.note: a yen is a strong craving
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written as O
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A palace attendant is hungry enough to eat a duck along with his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird but is the cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen of the Guard are the British monarch's ceremonial bodyguard, so a yeoman is a servant of the Crown.

clue.text: Accomplished detective with too much to do

parts.note: a job accomplished is over and done
busy is old British slang for a police detective

explanation.surface: A capable sleuth is swamped with work.
explanation.definitionFit: Overloaded with tasks is a synonym for having too much to do.

clue.text: Ability to make sense of ciphers?

definitions.text: Ability to make sense of ciphers?

parts.words: Ability to make sense of ciphers?
parts.note: ciphers suggest secret codes, but a cipher is also an old word for a numeral, so this means skill with figures

explanation.surface: A codebreaker's knack for cracking secret messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ciphers' tempts you towards codebreaking; here it means the digits 0 to 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Competence with numbers is the counterpart of literacy, the skill of handling figures.

clue.text: They have a will to distribute what is left

definitions.text: They have a will to distribute what is left

parts.words: They have a will to distribute what is left
parts.note: reads as people determined to share out leftovers, but it means those named in a will who hand out an estate

explanation.surface: Determined people share out the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as determination, but it is a legal testament; 'what is left' is what a dead person bequeaths.
explanation.definitionFit: People appointed to carry out a testament and share out the estate hold this legal role.

clue.text: Medieval writer, one economical with the truth

definitions.meaning: an author of medieval verse tales of chivalry
a person who embellishes or invents stories, a fibber

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an author of chivalric tales and someone who makes things up.

clue.text: Bare bones of poet gone into by Head of English

indicators.note: the poet's name is entered by another letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An English department chief delves into the essentials of a poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes E from English, and 'gone into by' puts it inside SKELTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework or outline reduced to essentials is called the skeleton, as bones are the frame of a body.

clue.text: Angry about seeds initially scattered

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry word goes round the letter

parts.note: going spare is British slang for being furious

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener is cross over the seeds that were scattered at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from seeds, and 'about' puts it inside SPARE. 'Spare' as angry is British, as in 'my mum will go spare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse growth is thinly scattered rather than dense.

clue.text: Way to secure old record with note on music

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the way encloses the other pieces

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
an EP, an extended-play disc, is a record format of the past
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A road keeps an old vinyl disc, with a written comment on the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music' is the definition: a septet is a composition for seven performers. 'with' and 'on' are only joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for seven players or voices is a piece of music of that name.

clue.text: Light-fingered East Ender's source of drink?

definitions.meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for a thief, as used in London's East End
dried leaves infused to make a cup of tea

explanation.definitionFit: The word is Cockney rhyming slang for thief and also the leaf a brew of tea comes from.

clue.text: Fellow follows saint of Balkan descent

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so the fellow comes after the saint

parts.note: St Alban was Britain's first Christian martyr
Ian is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man trails behind a holy figure with roots in south-east Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan country, so a person born there has Balkan origins.

clue.text: Upset over there, a high-class liqueur

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: yon is an old word for over there
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Sad about the posh drink being served across the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' gives NOY. 'U' for upper-class comes from a 1950s British essay dividing U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy flavoured with fruit kernels is a French liqueur of this name.

clue.text: Girl rejected by proper governess in Spain

parts.note: due means fitting or proper, as in due respect

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is turned down by a respectable Spanish governess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives NNA. A duenna is the chaperone of girls in a Spanish household.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls in a Spanish family has this Spanish title.

clue.text: Operatic heroine not quite right in the head?

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so drop the last letter

parts.note: sane people are normal, right in the head

explanation.surface: A diva who is not entirely sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' removes the final L of NORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's opera features a druid priestess as its title role.

clue.text: Some London celebrity, at some time in the past

definitions.text: at some time in the past

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A London star who was famous back in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at a time long gone.

clue.text: Impertinent sons imprisoned by state

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so the sons sit within the state

parts.note: to state something is to say it
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Cheeky lads have been locked up by the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, but it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheeky or saucy is the sense here, a synonym of insolent.

clue.text: Meeting to study pursuit of game

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
coursing is hunting hares with dogs by sight, and a course is such a chase

explanation.surface: A gathering called to examine the hunting of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse of people is a crowd or assembly, a coming together.

clue.text: Pole taking lodgings by Welsh river

parts.note: quarters are rooms where one lodges
the Taff flows through Cardiff in Wales

explanation.surface: A man from Poland takes rooms beside a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a long stick. 'taking' and 'by' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden staff used as a weapon in old English fighting is a kind of pole.
